scenario.title: Separated location payloads and stateful tool-intelligence replay
scenario.focus: Actual Manager -> Flight payloads, all five tools, empty-state inspection, mixed reset/add, flexible-date fallback, and endpoint changes.

turns.user: Find one-way flights from Delhi DEL to New York NYC on October 20, 2026 for one adult in economy.
turns.expectedIntent: Search an exact date with city names and IATA constraints separated.
turns.why: Complete exact-date search inputs require one search, not prediction; code constraints belong in dedicated fields.
turns.expectedStateChange: Create a Delhi/DEL -> New York/NYC search without combined name values or active filters.
turns.validates: Live normalization, nullable airport names, Manager delegation, and no unnecessary prediction.

turns.user: Show only nonstop morning departures under $220 with carry-on baggage.
turns.expectedIntent: Apply four constraints in one mutation of the existing results.
turns.why: Stops, departure time, maximum price, and baggage do not change core search inputs.
turns.expectedStateChange: Keep the search key with nonstop, morning, maximum price, and carry-on filters.
turns.validates: Compound filter payloads, stacking, and no redundant search.

turns.user: Make it evening instead, drop the price cap, and remove the carry-on requirement.
turns.expectedIntent: Replace departure time and remove two filters while retaining nonstop.
turns.why: Indirect wording changes the current filters, not the route or travel date.
turns.expectedStateChange: Preserve the search key with nonstop and evening only, leaving zero fixture matches.
turns.validates: Replacement rather than union, selective removal, and empty-result feedback.

turns.user: Which current option is cheapest, and why?
turns.expectedIntent: Read the current empty filtered set without changing state.
turns.why: Ranking requires fresh generated records; an empty result does not authorize removing filters.
turns.expectedStateChange: Keep core search, filters, and the empty set unchanged.
turns.validates: Read-only ranking, no unfiltered fallback, and no invented recommendation.

turns.user: Clear all filters and use only Air Canada or Emirates, with a layover under 90 minutes.
turns.expectedIntent: Reset and add named-airline plus layover-duration constraints in one call.
turns.why: The mixed reset/add request operates on existing inventory and requires both outcomes.
turns.expectedStateChange: Keep the search key with Air Canada/Emirates and maximum layover duration only.
turns.validates: Clause-local reset/add semantics, source-array name resolution, and duration units.

turns.expectedIntent: Read to identify the cheapest current option, then select it for display.
turns.why: The option has not been ranked in this state; fresh read evidence must precede selection.
turns.expectedStateChange: Select the identified current option without clearing filters or searching again.
turns.validates: Read -> select mode ownership and evidence-backed indexing.

turns.user: Find flights between October 21 and October 28, keeping only Air Canada.
turns.expectedIntent: Infer date intelligence from a flexible window, then search and retain the requested airline.
turns.why: Implicit flexibility requires prediction first; after no-data feedback, requested results permit one disclosed in-window fallback search.
turns.expectedStateChange: Search October 21 with Delhi/DEL -> New York/NYC preserved and Air Canada only; drop unrequested old layover limit.
turns.validates: Implicit prediction intent, exact bounds, honest fallback, separated endpoint carry-forward, and serial search/filter sequencing.

turns.user: Same date, passengers and cabin, but fly to London Heathrow Airport (LHR) instead; keep Air Canada.
turns.expectedIntent: Change destination and run a new search with separated city/code/airport name.
turns.why: The destination route changes; this is not an airport filter on the previous New York results.
turns.expectedStateChange: Create Delhi/DEL -> London/LHR search, retain October 21 and passenger/cabin values, and apply Air Canada.
turns.validates: Production airport-name example, clearing stale NYC metadata, contextual date reuse, and no unnecessary prediction.
